SMTO-JOB-0011 — A background command can't use input sent during the task

GUID: d54e7471-d4cd-4a03-bb91-f3a28b711a48
Slug: job-input-not-durable
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • The agent tried to start a command as a background job and also hand it some input text directly. A background job can't keep input handed over that way, so SMTO refused it. The command did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the agent continue; it usually puts the input into the command itself or into a file, then starts the background job again. A background job can read input saved that way at any time, even after the conversation moves on.
  2. If the command must be handed its input as it starts, ask the agent to run it as a normal command that you wait for, not in the background. Only a normal run can be handed input directly when it starts.
  3. If the input includes a password or other secret, don't ask the agent to write it into a file or into the command. Files and command text can end up in logs, where a secret shouldn't be kept.

What success looks like

  • The command starts, and the task shows it running in the background or shows its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same command unchanged; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A managed job launch (background=true, execution_mode tty/BatchModeTTY/BatchModeNoTTY, or an external-skill job) was requested with stdin_mode literal or input_binding; a durable job cannot keep task-supplied standard input, so the call was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • Effective background execution is selected while stdin_mode is not none, because this durable-job path cannot retain task-owned transient stdin. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • Effective background execution is selected while stdin_mode is not none, because this durable-job path cannot retain task-owned transient stdin.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect effective background selection and stdin_mode; command-owned heredoc/file input has a separate durable lifetime.

How to fix it

  • Managed job launches require stdin_mode=none: put the input in a command-owned heredoc or a file on the Gateway, or for interactive prompts use BatchModeTTY and answer through manage_job action=input. Otherwise run the call in the default captured mode without background, where stdin_mode literal or input_binding is accepted. Keep secrets in supported private input channels, not in command text or files.
  • Put the intended task input in a command-owned heredoc or supported file before launching a durable job. Keep secrets in supported private channels.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended background command owns its supported persistent input and passes ordinary private-data controls.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
